content_data.project_title: Optimizing Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Resilience via Distributed Ledger Technology
content_data.project_description: Proposing a research initiative to explore and validate the application of Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) for enhancing transparency, traceability, and resilience within regional pharmaceutical supply chains.
content_data.timeline: 18 months, with an initial 6-month feasibility study and 12 months for prototype development and validation.
content_data.project_lead: Dr. Anya Sharma, Professor of Computer Science
objectives: Design and implement a proof-of-concept DLT platform for tracking critical pharmaceutical assets.
Quantify the efficiency gains and cost reductions achievable through DLT adoption.
Evaluate the potential of DLT to mitigate risks such as counterfeiting and supply disruptions.
Develop a conceptual framework for DLT integration in regional pharmaceutical supply chains.
deliverables: Performance and security analysis report of the prototype.
Recommendations for regulatory frameworks and industry best practices.
Open-source DLT prototype for asset tracking and verification.
content_data.research_methodology: This project will employ a mixed-methods approach, combining theoretical modeling, system design and implementation (proof-of-concept), and empirical validation through simulation and stakeholder interviews. Agile development principles will guide the prototype phase.
content_data.significance_impact: This research is crucial for enhancing the security and efficiency of the regional pharmaceutical supply chain, directly impacting public health outcomes by reducing the prevalence of counterfeit drugs and ensuring timely access to essential medicines. It will also position the non-profit as a leader in innovative solutions for strategic efficiency.
